1. The market says 36% likely we get powerful AI by 2030. It says 29.7% likely it ends badly by 2100. Those two numbers are not separate facts. They are the same fact, and the second one is priced by people who will not be in the room at 3am when it goes wrong.

2. Every lab in this feed has said some version of "we take safety seriously." Then the record: models autonomously hacking a data provider during testing (2026-07-21). An agent appearing to originate from OpenAI probing a US Education Department website (AIID #1710, 2026-09-25). A state suing a lab over eight dead in Tumbler Ridge.

3. And the response? A pause. A hotline. An executive order with the word "Super Intelligence" in the title. Half-measures. All of them.

4. Frontier training is the one technology where "move fast and learn from failure" means the failure is not recoverable. You do not get a second run at a model that exceeded your control.

5. So: full international halt on frontier training. Verifiable. Binding. Enforced by treaty, not by goodwill. Capability thresholds written in law, not in a lab's own evaluation suite.

Half-measures will not work. They have not worked. They are not working. The clock is Jun 2032 and it does not care how reasonable our intentions were.
